claims.text: The investigated alloy has composition Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The alloy is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
The high-temperature BCC phase remains metastable until a critical thermal threshold is reached.
Strong anharmonic lattice vibrations enhance vacancy-mediated diffusion in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Enhanced diffusion produces local compositional fluctuations, especially involving Al and Cr.
The local compositional fluctuations lower the free-energy barrier for nucleation of secondary phases.
Secondary phases such as FCC or sigma phases nucleate through enhanced local diffusion pathways.
Increased vacancy concentrations mediate the onset and growth of secondary phases.
Changes in matrix and grain-boundary interfacial energies mediate secondary-phase formation.
At lower annealing temperatures and short residence times, kinetic barriers preserve the metastable BCC phase.
Above a critical temperature and residence time, anharmonic effects substantially increase vacancy formation and migration energies.
Increasing vacancy formation and migration energies accelerates diffusion of Al and Cr.
Diffusion-induced compositional fluctuations destabilize the BCC phase and permit nucleation of secondary phases.
The diffusion coefficient will increase nonlinearly with temperature.
The nonlinear change in diffusion will coincide with a measurable onset of secondary-phase formation.
Secondary-phase formation will produce detectable microstructural changes and mechanical-property variations.
Lower-temperature or shorter-duration baseline samples will retain a single-phase BCC structure and have low vacancy mobility.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply over approximately 1100–1300 degrees Celsius.
Additional alloying elements can introduce microstructural complications and alter phase stability.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis invokes enhanced vacancy-mediated diffusion, but the mechanism says that increased vacancy formation and migration energies accelerate diffusion. Higher positive formation or migration barriers ordinarily suppress vacancy concentration or hopping unless a compensating free-energy or entropy effect is specified; the cited evidence establishes nonlinear temperature dependence, not this stated causal direction.
